items.title: Node-graph execution ontology

items.title: Governance roles and runtime authority

items.title: Completion and promotion states remain distinct

items.title: Shared provider-runtime actor envelope
items.statement: Requested/effective provider identity and tool, role, selection-reason, and PRD/account lineage concepts span assistant, interviewer, builders, overseers, node workers, and other provider-backed turns without merging actor ontologies.

evidence.exact_quote: The shared provider-runtime contract applies beyond Orchestrator: `Multi-Account.md` governs assistant, interviewer, requirements builder, PRD builder, overseers, node workers, and provider-backed chat/tool turns. items.title: Canonical labels and weak-integration presentation
items.statement: User-facing consumers must use the canonical object/action labels; Seams UI visibly summarizes weak integration, groups it into readable categories, and exposes blocked reason, owner, and recovery context.

evidence.exact_quote: Canonical copy favors precise runtime and user-facing labels. Object/action labels include `Seams`, `Feature Seam`, `Work Package`, `Package Overseer`, `Seam Overseer`, `Locally Complete`, `Seam Complete`, `Completion Blocked`, `Weak Integration`, `Promotion Blocked`, `Promotion Revoked`, `Corroboration Requested`, `Challenge Accepted`, `Challenge Not Accepted`, `Advisory Concern Recorded`, `Graph Patch Requested`, `Graph Patch Applied`, and `Generation Updated`; `/labels`, `/action`, `/runtime`, and `/object` consumers must not invent alternate peer terms.

Weak integration is not just a badge. Seams UI must summarize weak integration visibly and group concerns under readable headings such as Wiring, Workflow, State, GUI, and Design. Package issues roll up to seam concerns only when they cross package-to-seam, `/seam/user-visible`, or user-visible boundaries or affect seam completion truth. `Locally Complete`, `Available to Seam`, and `Seam Complete` remain distinct from `Lane to Package`, `Package to Seam`, and `Seam Completion` promotion boundaries.

Revocation and reopen semantics are explicit named states: `Promotion Revoked`, `Seam Completion Revoked`, `Reopened`, `Reopened by Patch`, and `Reopened by New Evidence`. Blocked states expose blocked reason, blocked owner, and recovery context. Weak-integration buckets include missing GUI representation of runtime/governance state, state-model mismatch across package boundaries, user-flow dead ends or partial affordances, contract drift, duplicated interpretation across packages, technically passing local checks while seam-level UX or architecture remains poor, GUI/runtime mismatch, incomplete end-to-end flow, cross-package state mismatch, local-pass/global-fail composition, missing degraded `/recovery` behavior, inconsistent UX semantics, cross-seam architecture drift, and invisible governance or missing operator affordances. `Decision_Policy` needs first-class policy objects and transitions for concerns, corroboration, promotions, and superseded `/revoked/reopened` states.

dimension_assessments.summary: The window records explicit decision behaviors for graph orchestration, governance, completion, corroboration, graph patching, approvals, navigation, evidence capture, and cleanup retention.
First-class weak-integration governance, actor audit/replay, navigation, and lineage capabilities are asserted.
Approval identity inputs are named, but navigation payloads and failure outputs are not specified.
Core contracts and exact labels are present, but corroboration and actor-envelope schemas remain materially under-specified.
Completion, promotion, revocation, reopen, generation, and retained states are named, but transition tables and lifecycle exits are absent.
The window explicitly assigns decision-log authority, runtime governance authority, graph ownership, and canonical navigation identities.
Decision_Log ownership and cross-document ContractRef routing are explicit, with PlanUnit owner and implementation surfaces preserved.
Runtime, GUI, object/action label consumers, provider-backed actors, and cross-document consumers are named.
Visible labels and weak-integration presentation are explicit, but the completion PlanUnit is classified non-GUI despite user-facing completion truth and GUI implementation surfaces.
Blocked-state recovery context and degraded-recovery categories are recognized, but transition recovery, retained cleanup recovery, and navigation failure contracts are not closed.
Debug capture has a clear secret/PII boundary, but the shared actor envelope lacks redaction and persistence-minimization rules for auth/account context.
ContractRefs, owner/consumer routing, graph lineage, and seam rollup describe propagation, while GUI classification and rollup clearing gaps threaten consistent downstream propagation.
Runtime owns retries and dispatch and lanes can be retained, but retry limits, retention reevaluation, cleanup recovery, and operational scale controls are unstated.
No measurable bounds or performance oracle are supplied for full graphs, generations, lineage, rollups, or actor replay.
Request-centric to blocked-episode approval migration and alias-only compatibility boundaries are explicitly retained.
PlanUnits provide prose acceptance criteria and structural validators, but no behavior-specific executable receipts for the runtime and GUI decisions.
Consequential discretion remains in corroboration operands, envelope schema, state transitions, GUI classification, retention, rollup, navigation failures, scale, and semantic tests.
The main unknowns are the unclosed schemas, transition guards, lifecycle exits, aggregation semantics, failure outputs, and performance budgets identified by this window review.
